thread:
Mira: Heads up — our Next.js edge sample is failing on Vercel edge runtime with 'require is not defined'. Anyone seen this pattern before? :eyes:
Devlin: Which package.json did the sample install? local vs published?
Mira: Published 0.7.3. Repro steps in the sample app: import { RedwoodClient } from 'redwood-inference'; page render crashes during edge init.
Ashok: Likely we shipped CJS as the default export resolution. Edge runtimes are ESM-only and error on require().
Zane: Can you paste the exports section?
Mira: Sure, snippet from 0.7.3:
```
"exports": {
  ".": "./dist/cjs/index.js",
  "./package.json": "./package.json"
}
```
Devlin: Ouch — that forces consumers to the CJS entry. Bundlers that use 'import' may still pick esm, but Vercel edge used runtime import() which hit package exports and got cjs.
Katy: This is the classic dual-package dilemma. We have ESM build but our exports fallback points to cjs. Need conditional exports.
Ashok: Two big constraints: 1) Node resolver supports conditional 'import'/'require' keys, 2) TypeScript resolves types via the top-level 'types' field (or typesVersions), not via exports in many TS versions.
Zane: Proposed exports map (rough):
```
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "import": "./dist/esm/index.mjs",
    "require": "./dist/cjs/index.cjs"
  }
}
"main": "./dist/cjs/index.cjs",
"module": "./dist/esm/index.mjs",
"types": "./dist/esm/index.d.ts",
```
Katy: That looks fine but "types" at the top-level is required. Some older TS won't follow conditional types inside exports. We should ship a flat d.ts at dist/index.d.ts and point "types" to that for maximum compatibility.
Mira: Also question about "type": "module" at package root — if we set that, Node treats .js as ESM which breaks require consumers unless we ship .cjs files.
Devlin: So build outputs should be: dist/esm/index.mjs, dist/cjs/index.cjs, dist/index.d.ts (or dist/esm/index.d.ts + copy to dist/index.d.ts).
Ashok: Another nuance: Edge runtimes (Vercel/Cloudflare) sometimes require a separate edge entry because they don't support Node builtins or certain sync APIs. We might need an "edge" entrypoint with a very small wrapper.
Zane: We could add an export condition like "worker" or "edge" but that's nonstandard — most resolvers ignore custom conditions. Better to document an explicit import path: import from 'redwood-inference/edge' or 'redwood-inference/esm' for samples.
Katy: For DX: we should make the default import work for the majority: conditional exports with import/require, top-level types, and CI test matrix covering Next.js edge, Vite, Bun, and Node 14/16/18.
Mira: Short-term hotfix: publish patch where exports has import->esm and require->cjs plus top-level "main" -> cjs and "module" -> esm and a flat "types". That should unblock the sample.
Devlin: I can draft a tiny RFC with examples and build script changes. Plan: change rollup/tsc output to emit .mjs/.cjs, copy .d.ts to dist root, add sample apps under /examples/edge-next and /examples/cjs, and add (fast) CI jobs.
Ashok: Also add a tiny runtime shim to the edge sample that uses dynamic import to avoid require usage during build. Might be useful as a sample pattern.
Mira: Agree. Can we also bump our minimum TS version in repo or at least call out supported TS versions in README? Some users with TS 4.6 will still get weird type resolution.
Zane: Yep. Add compatibility matrix to the RFC. I'll draft tests for Vite and Next edge.
Katy: Action items summary:
- Devlin: draft RFC + package.json export proposal
- Ashok: update build to output .mjs/.cjs and copy d.ts to dist root
- Zane: add CI jobs for Edge/Vite/Bun matrices and sample app adjustments
- Mira: patch release to unblock customers, update sample app and docs
Devlin: I'll start the RFC tonight and tag everyone. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: CI pipeline 'examples-edge' failed on 1 test — reproducer in ci/artifacts/edge-failure.log
Mira: Thanks, @deploy-bot — I'll grab the logs and try the patch locally.
Katy: One last thing — let's keep the public API surface stable. Avoid exposing internal edge-only helpers unless we want them supported.
Mira: Agreed. OK moving to RFC + patch cadence. Thanks all. :rocket:
